sanskrit: praviśya tu mahāraṇyaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyam ātmavān dadarśa rāmo durdharṣas tāpasāśramamaṇḍalam
english: Entering the great forest, the Daṇḍaka wilderness, the self-possessed and invincible Rāma beheld the precinct of the ascetics' hermitage.

sanskrit: kuśacīraparikṣiptaṃ brāhmyā lakṣmyā samāvṛtam yathā pradīptaṃ durdharśaṃ gagane sūryamaṇḍalam
english: Surrounded by kuśa grass and bark cloth, pervaded by the radiance of Brahmā, it blazed forth, difficult to behold — like the disk of the sun flaming in the sky.

sanskrit: śaraṇyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ susamṛṣṭājiraṃ sadā pūjitaṃ copanṛttaṃ ca nityam apsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: It was a refuge for all beings, its courtyard always well-swept, perpetually honored and danced upon by troops of Apsarases.

sanskrit: viśālair agniśaraṇaiḥ srugbhāṇḍair ajinaiḥ kuśaiḥ samidbhis toyakalaśaiḥ phalamūlaiś ca śobhitam
english: It was adorned with broad fire-shelters, sacrificial ladles and vessels, antelope skins, kuśa grass, sacred fuel, water-pots, fruits and roots.

sanskrit: āraṇyaiś ca mahāvṛkṣaiḥ puṇyaiḥ svāduphalair vṛtam balihomārcitaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam
english: Ringed with great forest trees bearing auspicious sweet fruits, consecrated by bali offerings and fire-oblations, holy and resounding with the chanting of the Veda.

sanskrit: puṣpair vanyaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ padminyā ca sapadmayā phalamūlāśanair dāntaiś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraiḥ
english: Encircled by wild flowers and a lotus-pond thick with blooms, inhabited by self-restrained ascetics subsisting on fruits and roots, clad in bark cloth and black antelope hides.

sanskrit: sūryavaiśvānarābhaiś ca purāṇair munibhir vṛtam puṇyaiś a niyatāhāraiḥ śobhitaṃ paramarṣibhiḥ
english: Surrounded by ancient sages effulgent as the sun and fire, adorned by great seers of controlled diet and holy conduct.

sanskrit: tad brahmabhavanaprakhyaṃ brahmaghoṣanināditam brahmavidbhir mahābhāgair brāhmaṇair upaśobhitam
english: That place resembled the abode of Brahmā, reverberating with Vedic recitation, beautified by blessed brāhmaṇas who knew Brahman.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmāṃs tāpasāśramamaṇḍalam abhyagacchan mahātejā vijyaṃ kṛtvā mahad dhanuḥ
english: Beholding that precinct of the ascetics' hermitage, the glorious Rāghava of great splendor strung his great bow and advanced.

sanskrit: divyajñānopapannās te rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā maharṣayaḥ abhyagacchaṃs tadā prītā vaidehīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
english: Those great seers, possessed of divine knowledge, seeing Rāma, came forward joyfully to meet him and the illustrious Vaidehī as well.

sanskrit: te taṃ somam ivodyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇaḥ maṅgalāni prayuñjānāḥ pratyagṛhṇan dṛḍhavratāḥ
english: Those walkers of righteousness, firm in their vows, beholding him like the rising moon, pronouncing auspicious blessings, received him with honor.

sanskrit: rūpasaṃhananaṃ lakṣmīṃ saukumāryaṃ suveṣatām dadṛśur vismitākārā rāmasya vanavāsinaḥ
english: The forest-dwelling ascetics gazed in wonder at Rāma's physical form, his noble bearing, his beauty, his delicacy, and the grace of his appearance.

sanskrit: vaidehīṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmaṃ netrair animiṣair iva āścaryabhūtān dadṛśuḥ sarve te vanacāriṇaḥ
english: All those forest wanderers beheld Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa, and Rāma with eyes that seemed not to blink, as though gazing at marvels.

sanskrit: atrainaṃ hi mahābhāgāḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ atithiṃ parṇaśālāyāṃ rāghavaṃ saṃnyaveśayan
english: There the blessed ones, devoted to the welfare of all beings, lodged Rāghava as a guest in the leaf-thatched hall.

sanskrit: tato rāmasya satkṛtya vidhinā pāvakopamāḥ ājahrus te mahābhāgāḥ salilaṃ dharmacāriṇaḥ
english: Then those blessed sages, blazing like fire, walkers of righteousness, having duly honored Rāma with proper rites, brought water for him.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vanyam āśramaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ nivedayītvā dharmajñās tataḥ prāñjalayo 'bruvan
english: Having offered roots, flowers, forest fruits and the hermitage to the great-souled one, those knowers of dharma then spoke with joined palms.

sanskrit: dharmapālo janasyāsya śaraṇyaś ca mahāyaśāḥ pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca rājā daṇḍadharo guruḥ
english: "The king is protector of the dharma of his people, refuge of the greatly renowned, worthy of worship and of honor, the wielder of the rod of justice, the master."

sanskrit: indrasyaiva caturbhāgaḥ prajā rakṣati rāghava rājā tasmād vanān bhogān bhuṅkte lokanamaskṛtaḥ
english: "A king who protects his subjects receives a fourth share of Indra's merit, O Rāghava; therefore the king, honored by all the world, enjoys wealth even from forests."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ bhavatā rakṣyā bhavadviṣayavāsinaḥ nagarastho vanastho vā tvaṃ no rājā janeśvaraḥ
english: "We dwell within your domain and must be protected by you; whether you reside in the city or the forest, you are our king and lord of the people."

sanskrit: nyastadaṇḍā vayaṃ rājañ jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ rakṣitavyās tvayā śaśvad garbhabhūtās tapodhanāḥ
english: "We who have laid down the rod, conquered anger, and mastered our senses — we ascetics whose wealth is austerity — must always be protected by you as though we were in the womb."

sanskrit: evam uktvā phalair mūlaiḥ puṣpair vanyaiś ca rāghavam anyaiś ca vividhāhāraiḥ salakṣmaṇam apūjayan
english: Having spoken thus, they honored Rāghava along with Lakṣmaṇa with fruits, roots, wild flowers, and various other foods.

sanskrit: tathānye tāpasāḥ siddhā rāmaṃ vaiśvānaropamāḥ nyāyavṛttā yathānyāyaṃ tarpayām āsur īśvaram
english: Other accomplished ascetics, blazing like Vaiśvānara fire, righteous in conduct, likewise gratified the lordly Rāma in proper fashion.

sanskrit: kṛtātithyo 'tha rāmas tu sūryasyodayanaṃ prati āmantrya sa munīn sarvān vanam evānvagāhata
english: Rāma, having been duly received as a guest, then, toward the rising of the sun, took leave of all the sages and plunged into the forest.

sanskrit: nānāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ śārdūlavṛkasevitam dhvastavṛkṣalatāgulmaṃ durdarśa salilāśayam
english: Crowded with herds of various animals, frequented by tigers and wolves, its trees, creepers and thickets fallen and broken, its pools of water hard to see.

sanskrit: niṣkūjanānāśakuni jhillikā gaṇanāditam lakṣmaṇānugato rāmo vanamadhyaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, beheld the interior of that forest bereft of calling birds, but resounding with the cries of swarms of crickets.

sanskrit: vanamadhye tu kākutsthas tasmin ghoramṛgāyute dadarśa giriśṛṅgābhaṃ puruṣādaṃ mahāsvanam
english: In the midst of that forest filled with fearsome beasts, Kākutstha encountered a man-eater, tall as a mountain peak, roaring with a mighty voice.

sanskrit: gabhīrākṣaṃ mahāvaktraṃ vikaṭaṃ viṣamodaram bībhatsaṃ viṣamaṃ dīrghaṃ vikṛtaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Deep-eyed, vast-mouthed, misshapen, with a belly like a poison-pot — repulsive, uneven, towering, grotesque, and terrible to behold.

sanskrit: vasānaṃ carmavaiyāghraṃ vasārdraṃ rudhirokṣitam trāsanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ vyāditāsyam ivāntakam
english: He was clad in a tiger skin soaked in fat and drenched in blood, his gaping mouth inspiring terror in all creatures — like Death itself with jaws flung wide.

sanskrit: trīn siṃhāṃś caturo vyāghrān dvau vṛkau pṛṣatān daśa saviṣāṇaṃ vasādigdhaṃ gajasya ca śiro mahat
english: Three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten spotted deer, and the great head of an elephant with its tusks, all smeared with marrow and fat —

sanskrit: avasajyāyase śūle vinadantaṃ mahāsvanam sa rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca maithilīm
english: — were hung upon an iron spit. That one, roaring with a great voice, upon seeing Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sītā the daughter of Maithilī —

sanskrit: abhyadhāvat susaṃkruddhaḥ prajāḥ kāla ivāntakaḥ sa kṛtvā bhairavaṃ nādaṃ cālayann iva medinīm
english: — rushed at them in violent fury like Death the Destroyer come for living creatures, uttering a fearsome roar as if shaking the very earth.

sanskrit: aṅgenādāya vaidehīm apakramya tato 'bravīt yuvāṃ jaṭācīradharau sabhāryau kṣīṇajīvitau
english: Seizing Vaidehī with one arm and withdrawing, he then spoke: "You two bear matted hair and bark cloth, yet travel with a wife — your lives are forfeit."

sanskrit: praviṣṭau daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ śaracāpāsidhāriṇau kathaṃ tāpasayor vāṃ ca vāsaḥ pramadayā saha
english: "You have entered the Daṇḍaka forest bearing arrows, bows and swords. How can two who pass as ascetics dwell here in the company of a woman?"

sanskrit: adharmacāriṇau pāpau kau yuvāṃ munidūṣakau ahaṃ vanam idaṃ durgaṃ virāgho nāma rākṣasaḥ
english: "Who are you two sinners, walkers of unrighteousness, defilers of sages? I am the Rākṣasa named Virādha, and this impenetrable forest is mine."

sanskrit: carāmi sāyudho nityam ṛṣimāṃsāni bhakṣayan iyaṃ nārī varārohā mama bharyā bhaviṣyati yuvayoḥ pāpayoś cāhaṃ pāsyāmi rudhiraṃ mṛdhe
english: "I roam here always, armed, devouring the flesh of sages. This woman of beautiful form shall become my wife, and I shall drink the blood of you two sinners in battle."

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ bruvato dhṛṣṭaṃ virādhasya durātmanaḥ śrutvā sagarvitaṃ vākyaṃ saṃbhrāntā janakātmajā sītā prāvepatodvegāt pravāte kadalī yathā
english: Hearing the arrogant and boastful words thus spoken by the evil-souled Virādha, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, became distraught and trembled with anguish like a plantain tree in the wind.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītāṃ virādhāṅkagatāṃ śubhām abravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Seeing the lovely Sītā clutched in Virādha's embrace, Rāghava spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, his face parched with grief.

sanskrit: paśya saumya narendrasya janakasyātmasaṃbhavām mama bhāryāṃ śubhācārāṃ virādhāṅke praveśitām atyanta sukhasaṃvṛddhāṃ rājaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: "See, dear Saumya, the daughter of King Janaka, my wife, virtuous in conduct, the illustrious princess reared in the utmost comfort — now placed in Virādha's lap."

sanskrit: yad abhipretam asmāsu priyaṃ vara vṛtaṃ ca yat kaikeyyās tu susaṃvṛttaṃ kṣipram adyaiva lakṣmaṇa
english: "Whatever was intended against us, whatever boon was sought and obtained — all of Kaikeyī's scheming has come to swift fruition this very day, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: yā na tuṣyati rājyena putrārthe dīrghadarśinī yayāhaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ hitaḥ prasthāpito vanam adyedānīṃ sakāmā sā yā mātā mama madhyamā
english: "She who was not satisfied with the kingdom, that far-sighted one who had me — declared a blessing to all beings — sent to the forest for the sake of her son: that middle mother of mine has now achieved her desire."

sanskrit: parasparśāt tu vaidehyā na duḥkhataram asti me pitur vināśāt saumitre svarājyaharaṇāt tathā
english: "O Saumitre, there is no grief deeper for me than the touch of another man upon Vaidehī — not the death of my father, not the seizure of my rightful kingdom."

sanskrit: iti bruvati kākutsthe bāṣpaśokapariplute abravīl lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho ruddho nāga iva śvasan
english: As Kākutstha spoke thus, overwhelmed by tears and grief, Lakṣmaṇa, enraged, spoke — restrained, yet hissing like a great serpent.

sanskrit: anātha iva bhūtānāṃ nāthas tvaṃ vāsavopamaḥ mayā preṣyeṇa kākutstha kimarthaṃ paritapsyase
english: "You who are like Vāsava, the lord of all beings, why do you grieve as though you had no protector, O Kākutstha, when I, your servant, stand here?"

sanskrit: śareṇa nihatasyādya mayā kruddhena rakṣasaḥ virādhasya gatāsor hi mahī pāsyati śoṇitam
english: "Struck down today by my arrow in fury, the Rākṣasa Virādha, bereft of life, shall have the earth drink his blood."

sanskrit: rājyakāme mama krodho bharate yo babhūva ha taṃ virādhe vimokṣyāmi vajrī vajram ivācale
english: "The rage that was in me against Bharata, who coveted the kingdom — that I shall now release upon Virādha, as the wielder of the thunderbolt hurls his bolt upon a mountain."

sanskrit: mama bhujabalavegavegitaḥ patatu śaro 'sya mahān mahorasi vyapanayatu tanoś ca jīvitaṃ patatu tataś ca mahīṃ vighūrṇitaḥ
english: "Driven by the force and speed of my arm's strength, let a great arrow fall upon his broad chest, let it strip the life from his body, and let him then fall spinning to the earth."

sanskrit: athovāca punar vākyaṃ virādhaḥ pūrayan vanam ātmānaṃ pṛcchate brūtaṃ kau yuvāṃ kva gamiṣyathaḥ
english: Then Virādha spoke again, filling the forest with his voice, asking the two about themselves: "Tell me who you two are, and where you intend to go."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rāmo rākṣasaṃ jvalitānanam pṛcchantaṃ sumahātejā ikṣvākukulam ātmanaḥ
english: Then Rāma of very great splendor addressed the Rākṣasa with his blazing countenance as he questioned them, declaring his own lineage of Ikṣvāku.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo vṛttasaṃpannau viddhi nau vanagocarau tvāṃ tu veditum icchāvaḥ kas tvaṃ carasi daṇḍakān
english: "Know us as two Kṣatriyas endowed with proper conduct, roaming the forest. We, in turn, wish to know you: who are you, roaming the Daṇḍaka forest?"

sanskrit: tam uvāca virādhas tu rāmaṃ satyaparākramam hanta vakṣyāmi te rājan nibodha mama rāghava
english: Virādha then addressed Rāma of true valor: "Very well, I shall tell you, O king — hear what is mine, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: putraḥ kila jayasyāhaṃ mātā mama śatahradā virādha iti mām āhuḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvarākṣasāḥ
english: "I am the son of Jaya; my mother is Śatahradā. All Rākṣasas in the world call me Virādha."

sanskrit: tapasā cāpi me prāptā brahmaṇo hi prasādajā śastreṇāvadhyatā loke 'cchedyābhedyatvam eva ca
english: "By my austerities I have also obtained, by the grace of Brahmā, invulnerability to weapons in this world, and the quality of being neither cleavable nor pierceable."

sanskrit: utsṛjya pramadām enām anapekṣau yathāgatam tvaramāṇau pālayethāṃ na vāṃ jīvitam ādade
english: "Abandon this woman and flee the way you came, without a backward glance. I shall not take your lives — go, make haste and preserve yourselves."

sanskrit: taṃ rāmaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ rākṣasaṃ vikṛtākāraṃ virādhaṃ pāpacetasaṃ
english: Rāma, his eyes reddened with anger, replied to that Rākṣasa of misshapen form, Virādha of evil mind:

sanskrit: kṣudra dhik tvāṃ tu hīnārthaṃ mṛtyum anveṣase dhruvam raṇe saṃprāpsyase tiṣṭha na me jīvan gamiṣyasi
english: "Wretch! Shame on you, base creature — you seek death. You shall certainly find it in battle. Stand fast; you shall not leave me alive."

sanskrit: tataḥ sajyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā rāmaḥ suniśitāñ śarān suśīghram abhisaṃdhāya rākṣasaṃ nijaghāna ha
english: Then Rāma, stringing his bow, nocking razor-sharp arrows with great speed, struck the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: dhanuṣā jyāguṇavatā saptabāṇān mumoca ha rukmapuṅkhān mahāvegān suparṇānilatulyagān
english: He released seven arrows from his string-fitted bow — arrows with golden flights, of great velocity, swift as Suparṇa and the wind.

sanskrit: te śarīraṃ virādhasya bhittvā barhiṇavāsasaḥ nipetuḥ śoṇitādigdhā dharaṇyāṃ pāvakopamāḥ
english: Piercing the body of Virādha, who was clad in peacock feathers, those arrows fell to the ground drenched in blood, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: sa vinadya mahānādaṃ śūlaṃ śakradhvajopamam pragṛhyāśobhata tadā vyāttānana ivāntakaḥ
english: He — uttering a mighty roar — raised a pike tall as Indra's banner, and stood blazing forth like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: tac chūlaṃ vajrasaṃkāśaṃ gagane jvalanopamam dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ ciccheda rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: That pike, resembling a thunderbolt, blazing in the sky like fire — Rāma, foremost of weapon-bearers, split it asunder with two arrows.

sanskrit: tasya raudrasya saumitrir bāhuṃ savyaṃ babhañja ha rāmas tu dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ tarasā tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Saumitre broke the left arm of that fearsome being, while Rāma swiftly broke the right arm of the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sa bhagnabāhuḥ saṃvigno nipapātāśu rākṣasaḥ dharaṇyāṃ meghasaṃkāśo vajrabhinna ivācalaḥ idaṃ provāca kākutsthaṃ virādhaḥ puruṣarṣabham
english: His arms broken, the agitated Rākṣasa fell swiftly to the earth — like a cloud-mass, like a mountain split by the thunderbolt. Then Virādha spoke to Kākutstha, bull among men:

sanskrit: kausalyā suprajās tāta rāmas tvaṃ vidito mayā vaidehī ca mahābhāgā lakṣmaṇaś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: "Kausalyā is indeed blessed in her son — I recognize you, dear one: you are Rāma, and the greatly blessed Vaidehī, and the greatly glorious Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: abhiśāpād ahaṃ ghorāṃ praviṣṭo rākṣasīṃ tanum tumburur nāma gandharvaḥ śapto vaiśvaraṇena hi
english: "By a terrible curse I entered this Rākṣasa form — I am the Gandharva named Tumburu, cursed by Vaiśravaṇa."

sanskrit: prasādyamānaś ca mayā so 'bravīn māṃ mahāyaśāḥ yadā dāśarathī rāmas tvāṃ vadhiṣyati saṃyuge
english: "And when I sought to propitiate him, the greatly glorious one said to me: 'When Rāma, son of Daśaratha, slays you in battle —'"

sanskrit: tadā prakṛtim āpanno bhavān svargaṃ gamiṣyati iti vaiśravaṇo rājā rambhāsaktam uvāca ha
english: "'— then you shall regain your true nature and go to heaven.' Thus spoke King Vaiśravaṇa to me, who had been attached to the Apsarā Rambhā."

sanskrit: anupasthīyamāno māṃ saṃkruddho vyajahāra ha tava prasādān mukto 'ham abhiśāpāt sudāruṇāt bhavanaṃ svaṃ gamiṣyāmi svasti vo 'stu paraṃtapa
english: "When I did not attend upon him he became enraged and pronounced the curse. By your grace I am freed from this most dreadful curse; I shall now go to my own abode. May you be well, O scorcher of enemies."

sanskrit: ito vasati dharmātmā śarabhaṅgaḥ pratāpavān adhyardhayojane tāta maharṣiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaḥ
english: "Not far from here, a league and a half away, dwells the righteous and valiant great sage Śarabhaṅga, O dear one, blazing like the sun."

sanskrit: taṃ kṣipram abhigaccha tvaṃ sa te śreyo vidhāsyati avaṭe cāpi māṃ rāma nikṣipya kuśalī vraja
english: "Go to him swiftly; he will arrange what is best for you. And cast me into a pit, O Rāma, then depart in good health."

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ gatasattvānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ avaṭe ye nidhīyante teṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: "This is the eternal law for Rākṣasas who have departed life: those who are interred in a pit attain eternal worlds."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu kākutsthaṃ virādhaḥ śarapīḍitaḥ babhūva svargasaṃprāpto nyastadeho mahābalaḥ
english: Having thus addressed Kākutstha, Virādha, pierced by arrows, the mighty one, laid down his body and attained heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ muktakaṇṭham utkṣipya śaṅkukarṇaṃ mahāsvanam virādhaṃ prākṣipac chvabhre nadantaṃ bhairavasvanam
english: Lifting up that open-throated, spike-eared one roaring with a dreadful sound, they cast Virādha bellowing into a pit.

sanskrit: tatas tu tau kāñcanacitrakārmukau nihatya rakṣaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm vijahratus tau muditau mahāvane divi sthitau candradivākarāv iva
english: Then those two, bearing bows adorned with gold, having slain the Rākṣasa and taking Maithilī between them, roamed joyfully through the great forest — like the moon and sun standing together in the sky.
